description: issue #864 (review round 1): `tell` is a COMMAND, so it keeps its callable form -- the boundary that stops the new value-position rule from over-reaching. `spec/turtles-and-sprites.md`'s canonical-forms table is authoritative for the C3 Sprites rows and gives `tell <turtle|turtle-list>` Kind **C**, while `ask` and `each` are Kind **S**; `spec/grammar.md:408` names it in the same terms -- `the Sprites command tell -- a mode switch that takes no block`. `spec/grammar.md:390` matches a keyword as `callable-name` `only where the C3 primitive matrix also gives that word a callable form`, and a command HAS one, so `( tell :t )` is a legitimate `parenthesized-call` exactly as `( forward 5 )` is. The first revision of #864's rule rejected all seven profile words alike and turned this very source -- which checked CLEAN before the rule existed -- into an `ol-bad-token`; a review caught it, and this fixture is the stack-neutral guard so no future slice re-broadens the rule by accident. Both spellings are asserted in one program: the parenthesized call on line 2 and the bare statement form on line 4, each followed by a turtle command so the addressed-set change has something to apply to. Its Kind-S siblings in the same profile are asserted in `statement-heads-not-values`; the pair is what pins the rule to the C3 Kind column rather than to profile membership. NOTE: `print tell` -- `tell` in a genuine VALUE position -- is still undiagnosed, and that is a separate defect with a separate mechanism: `tell` reports no value and takes one input, so the honest finding is an arity/no-value one from `checker-arity.ts`, not a derivation error. Deliberately out of #864's scope and left unchanged. This is a check-mode fixture: it proves static legality only and does not execute.
